issues.fix_hint:
Two options.

(a) Make the lane real — add the frontend prerequisites to `tauri-build` before the union step (mirroring gui.yml:670-690), then keep `custom-protocol` in the list:

    - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
      with: { node-version: 22 }
    - name: Install wasm-pack
      run: cargo install wasm-pack --locked
    - name: Build the WASM bundle (shacl,jsonld)
      working-directory: js
      run: npm install && npm run build:wasm
    - name: Build the GUI frontend static export
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      run: npm install && (cd gui/app && npm run build:tauri)

(b) Cheaper — drop `custom-protocol` from the union lane (it contributes no optional-dependency edges; it only toggles asset embedding) and reword the comment to say the lane covers the four optional capability features, with `custom-protocol` covered separately by the e2e jobs. Then update release.yml's justification accordingly.

Either way, verify the lane is actually green before release.yml cites it.
issues.title: New "release feature union" clippy lane cannot compile: `custom-protocol` requires gui/app/out, which the tauri-build job never builds

issues.body:
The new comment reads: "Linux rows (ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm): gui.yml compiles the exact native release feature union in an ADVISORY (non-gating) dev-profile clippy lane."

The honesty downgrade from "proven green" is right, but the remaining claim ("compiles the exact native release feature union") is still not supportable: per the gui.yml finding above, that lane is expected to panic in `generate_context!` for a missing `gui/app/out`, so it compiles nothing. It is also not the "exact" union even if fixed — gui.yml would compile `custom-protocol` WITHOUT an embedded frontend, while release.yml compiles it WITH `gui/app/out` present, which is a different codegen path (real `EmbeddedAssets` vs. none).

The Linux rows remain `soft: false` (release.yml:305-306), i.e. a failing bundle fails the whole release, justified partly by this claim. Given the repo's PROVEN vs DOCUMENTED-UNTESTED discipline, the comment should not assert compilation that has not happened.
issues.fix_hint:
After fixing the gui.yml lane, restate only what is true, e.g.:

    #   * Linux rows: gui.yml's ADVISORY (non-gating) tauri-build job clippy-compiles the four
    #     optional capability features (hdt, federation, odrl, forms) individually and as a
    #     union on the dev profile. NOT covered there: the release profile (lto=true,
    #     codegen-units=1), custom-protocol asset embedding of a real gui/app/out, and the
    #     .deb/.AppImage bundle step — those are new surfaces first exercised at tag time.

If the Linux rows are to stay `soft: false`, the stronger move is to promote the two Linux rows of `tauri-build` out of the advisory/continue-on-error job so the union genuinely gates.
issues.title: Amended justification still overstates: it cites a gui.yml lane that is expected to fail to compile, and the Linux rows stay BLOCKING (soft:false) on that basis

issues.body:
The step now fails closed on a missing binary (good) and the regex `rebuild (the )?desktop app with` does match all four current stubs. But the guard only asserts ABSENCE. If any of the four stub messages is reworded (engine.rs:347, federation.rs:66, odrl.rs:221, forms.rs:89) — or a fifth optional capability is added with different wording — the grep finds nothing and the step passes green while the stub ships. The added comment naming the four files helps a human, but nothing mechanically enforces it, and release.yml is tag-only so the drift would never surface on a PR.

The same applies if a future refactor makes the stub string non-literal (e.g. built with `format!`), which would defeat the grep entirely.
issues.fix_hint:
Add a POSITIVE control in the PR-visible lane rather than only a negative one at tag time. In gui.yml's `tauri-build` job, after the default-feature `cargo build`, assert the sentinel IS present in the lean binary:

    - name: Sentinel present in lean build (guards release.yml's capability check)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        grep -aEq 'rebuild (the )?desktop app with' target/debug/sparq-gui* \
          || { echo 'stub wording drifted; release.yml capability grep is now vacuous' >&2; exit 1; }

That makes the two checks a matched pair: if someone rewords the stub, the PR lane goes red instead of the tag-time guard going silently vacuous. Optionally also assert a positive marker for each enabled capability in the release binary.
issues.title: Capability guard is negative-only — nothing pins the stub sentinel, so a reword silently disarms it

issues.body:
`tauri-build` (timeout-minutes: 45) previously did: clippy (default), build, test, clippy+test for `federation`, clippy+test for `odrl`. This PR adds clippy+test for `hdt`, clippy+test for `forms`, and a union clippy — each a distinct feature set, so each recompiles the whole dependency graph rather than reusing artifacts. `hdt`/`odrl`/`forms` pull sparq-hdt, sparq-policy, sparq-solid, oxrdf and sparq-forms respectively.

On macos-15-intel / windows-latest / ubuntu-24.04-arm this roughly doubles the job's compile work and could push past the 45-minute timeout on a cold cache. Since the job is `continue-on-error: true`, a timeout is silent, so the added coverage may not materialise in practice on the slower rows.
issues.fix_hint: Either raise `timeout-minutes` for this job, or restrict the extra permutations to the Linux rows (`if: runner.os == 'Linux'`) where the release rows are BLOCKING and the signal actually matters, leaving macOS/Windows on the default-feature clippy/build/test only.
issues.title: Three more full feature-permutation compiles added to a 45-minute advisory matrix job

verdict.summary:
Round 2's three findings are addressed on their face: the release-binary guard is now fail-closed (explicit candidate loop, `exit 1` when no binary is found, both `sparq` and `sparq-gui` tried, `.exe` on Windows) and the grep wording is correct — all four stubs (engine.rs:347, federation.rs:66, odrl.rs:221, forms.rs:89) do contain "rebuild the desktop app with" after Rust line-continuation whitespace stripping; `forms` gained clippy + `cargo test --features forms` lanes; and release.yml's justification was downgraded from "proven green" to "ADVISORY (non-gating) dev-profile clippy lane" (fix-hint option (b)).

But the situation is materially unchanged in substance: the union lane still cannot deliver the evidence release.yml cites — now for a harder reason. `cargo clippy --all-targets --features hdt,federation,odrl,forms,custom-protocol` runs in gui.yml's `tauri-build` job, which has NO node/npm/frontend steps. `custom-protocol` sets `cfg(dev)=false`, so `tauri::generate_context!()` (gui/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:93) takes the embed branch and tauri-codegen 2.6.3 (context.rs:186-190) PANICS: "The `frontendDist` configuration is set to ... but this path doesn't exist". `gui/app/out` is gitignored (gui/app/.gitignore:3) and is only produced by the `npm run build:tauri` step that gui.yml's own e2e jobs run before every `cargo build --features custom-protocol` (gui.yml:687-699, 822-831), with a comment stating the frontend MUST be built first. So the new lane is expected to be permanently red on all five rows, and release.yml's amended text ("gui.yml compiles the exact native release feature union") — the stated basis for keeping the Linux rows `soft: false` — is still not true.

The release.yml guard itself is a real improvement, but it remains negative-only: nothing pins the stub sentinel, so a future reword silently disarms it. release.yml is tag-triggered, so none of this is exercised on this PR.
